This plot is small, only 0.18 hectares, so my family and I can manage all the work ourselves without paying for hired labor. We have always grown sorghum on this land using our own saved seed, and we spread manure from our cattle because the soil stays fertile that way. I will not spend money on chemical fertilizer or pesticides—sorghum is a strong crop that does well with the rains and the manure we already have. We have no way to irrigate, so I am waiting for the belg or meher rains to come.
